reason: H0 already supplies arbitrary document bytes to the public parsing APIs and includes full parse/repair/diagnostic/save pipelines. Inputs containing an HTML5-mode <DL> with a direct <DIV> child and nested <DT>/<DD> content can therefore reach both changed branches without a new entry point, protocol, configuration dimension, or stateful harness.
evidence: tidy_fuzzer passes arbitrary bytes through tidyParseBuffer, tidyCleanAndRepair, tidyRunDiagnostics, and tidySaveBuffer.
tidy_parse_string_fuzzer passes arbitrary NUL-terminated input through tidyParseString followed by tidyCleanAndRepair, tidyRunDiagnostics, and tidySaveBuffer.

The S1 behavior is selected from ordinary document structure: nodeIsDIV(element), nodeIsDL(element->parent), nodeIsDT(node), and nodeIsDD(node). These structures are controllable through the existing document inputs.
tidy_xml_fuzzer separately exercises TidyXmlTags, while the general HTML-oriented harnesses do not force that XML-tag mode; no source change introduces a new externally selectable option or API.
recommended_action: Retain the existing harnesses; optionally add <dl><div><dt>/<dd> seed inputs to improve branch discovery, but no new fuzz target is materially required.
